scope.description: End-to-end witness on one real cluster: join a fresh, empty node through the public AddVoter API, record the suffrage the leader wrote for that member and the suffrage the new node itself sees, then take one original voter away and record whether a new command still commits - which it can only if the freshly added member counts as a voter.
assumptions: MakeCluster(2) plus MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1) merged and fully connected is the in-tree way to join a fresh node (raft_test.go:258-279), and the join itself is the public AddVoter call made by the elected leader.

Disconnecting one original voter is the discriminator: with three voters and one disconnected, a majority needs exactly the remaining original voter plus the new member, so a commit is only reachable if the new member votes; if the new member were the non-voting member the documentation describes, no majority would be reachable.
The apply future is waited on under a bounded interval because the completion of an accepted apply is not bounded by the caller's timeout.

basis.prefix: The harness (draft/assurance_generated_test.go) is one TestAssurance-prefixed test in the captured package. It bootstraps a real two-node cluster with MakeCluster(2, t, nil) and keeps a copy of the original members, creates a fresh single-node cluster with MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1, t, nil), merges the two clusters and fully connects them, then takes the elected leader with c.Leader() and the fresh node as the join target, identifying the other original voter as the peer to remove later. The join is the public leader.AddVoter(newNode.localID, newNode.localAddr, 0, 5s); its future is waited on under a bounded interval, recording add_err and, when it returned, the entry index it reports. The test then records the suffrage of the new member in the leader's latest configuration and in the new node's own latest configuration, and counts the voters in that configuration. It calls c.Disconnect on the other original voter's address and then applies one command through the public API, waiting on the apply future under a bounded interval and recording apply_with_one_original_voter_gone as committed, an error, or no_completion. Finally it records the new node's last index, the leader's state, and prints one CA_EVENT JSON line with all of these operands, so the decisive facts (the suffrage written for the added member, and whether a command can still commit with one original voter gone) come from the same cluster in one execution.
